adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:434 — Reusing existing Redis set keys with ZSCAN makes predeployment buffers raise WRONGTYPE and abort flushing whole batches until those keys expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis SET commands (sadd, scard, sscan) to SORTED SET commands (zadd, zcard, zscan) in buffer.py. The finding correctly identifies that during deployment, there will be a period where old SET keys created by the previous code version still exist in Redis. When the new code tries to use ZSCAN on these existing SET keys, Redis will return a WRONGTYPE error because ZSCAN only works on sorted sets, not regular sets. This is a real deployment compatibility issue - the code changes the data structure type but doesn't handle the transition period where both types may exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — Replaying a child span through an existing parent redirect sums its timestamp with the stored score, so eviction preserves replayed older spans and discards newer spans.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that 'zunionstore' sums timestamps when replaying a child span through an existing parent redirect. Looking at the diff, line 53 shows `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)`. The default behavior of ZUNIONSTORE in Redis is to use MAX aggregation when keys have the same member, not SUM. The diff does not specify an AGGREGATE option, so it uses the default MAX behavior. The finding incorrectly assumes SUM aggregation is being used. Additionally, the zpopmin at line 62 removes elements with the LOWEST scores (oldest timestamps), which is the correct behavior for evicting older spans, not newer ones as the finding suggests.

src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — ZADD and ZSCAN reuse keys previously populated by SADD, so existing buffered segments cause WRONGTYPE failures during deployment until drained or migrated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a migration from Redis SET commands (SADD, SSCAN, SCARD, SUNIONSTORE) to SORTED SET commands (ZADD, ZSCAN, ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE) in buffer.py and add-buffer.lua. The keys follow the pattern 'span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:span_id'. During deployment, existing data stored as SETs will still exist in Redis, but the new code will attempt to use SORTED SET operations on those keys. Redis will return WRONGTYPE errors when you try to use ZADD/ZSCAN on a key that contains a SET. This is a real deployment/migration issue - the code change doesn't include any migration strategy for existing data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — Replaying a child after its parent buffer merges sums its duplicate timestamp in ZUNIONSTORE, causing eviction to retain old spans ahead of newer spans.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZUNIONSTORE is used with 'AGGREGATE SUM' by default (line 53: `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)`). When a child span is replayed after its parent buffer has already merged, the same span payload would be added again with its timestamp score. ZUNIONSTORE with SUM aggregation would add the scores together, doubling the timestamp value for duplicate entries. This corrupted score would affect the zpopmin eviction logic (lines 61-63), potentially causing newer spans to be evicted instead of older ones since the duplicated span would have an artificially high score.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — The new hard-coded 1000-span eviction cap bypasses the still-exposed `max_segment_spans` setting, leaving a misleading no-op configuration and two divergent limits.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a hard-coded limit of 1000 spans in the Lua script (line 62: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call('zpopmin', set_key, span_count - 1000)`). Looking at buffer.py, there is indeed a `max_segment_spans` configuration that was previously used (lines 443-449 show code being removed that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`). The finding correctly identifies that the Lua script now enforces a hard-coded 1000 limit while the Python configuration `max_segment_spans` still exists but is no longer effective for this enforcement. This is a legitimate architectural concern about divergent/inconsistent limits, though not a bug per se since the system will still function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821 — OptimizedCursorPaginator` is a single-use subclass that copies nearly all of `BasePaginator.get_result`, so future cursor fixes must be kept in two implementations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that OptimizedCursorPaginator (lines 818-912 in paginator.py) duplicates most of the get_result logic from BasePaginator. Looking at the diff, the new class copies the entire pagination algorithm including cursor handling, offset calculation, and result building. This creates a maintenance burden where bug fixes to cursor pagination would need to be applied in two places. This is a legitimate architectural/maintainability concern grounded in the actual code added by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching live `span-buf:s:*` keys from Redis sets to sorted sets without a migration makes `ZADD` fail with `WRONGTYPE` for up to the one-hour TTL during rollout, causing background ingestion batches to fail until old buffers expire.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a clear change from Redis set operations (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to sorted set operations (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) in buffer.py and add-buffer.lua. The keys use the same naming pattern 'span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:span_id'. During deployment, existing keys created with set operations (SADD) will still exist with their TTL (set_timeout). When the new code tries to use ZADD on these existing set-type keys, Redis will return a WRONGTYPE error because you cannot use sorted set commands on regular set keys. This is a real migration issue that would cause failures during rollout until old keys expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — ZUNIONSTORE` uses Redis's default `SUM` aggregation, so an at-least-once retry of an already-buffered span inflates its timestamp score and can make the 1,000-span eviction discard newer legitimate spans instead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZUNIONSTORE being used at lines 47 and 52 in add-buffer.lua without specifying an aggregation method, which defaults to SUM in Redis. When the same span payload is processed multiple times (at-least-once delivery), its score (end_timestamp_precise) would be summed, artificially inflating it. Combined with the zpopmin eviction at line 59 that removes spans with the lowest scores, this could cause newer legitimate spans to be evicted instead of older ones, since the duplicated span would have an inflated score. This is a real correctness bug in the span buffering logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — No test inserts or merges more than 1,000 spans with distinct timestamps, so the new eviction branch's cap, boundary, and oldest-span ordering can regress without detection.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new eviction logic in add-buffer.lua at lines 55-62 that caps spans at 1000 and uses zpopmin to remove oldest spans when exceeded. Looking at the test files in the diff (test_buffer.py, test_flusher.py, test_consumer.py), none of the test cases insert more than a handful of spans (typically 4-5 spans per test). The finding correctly identifies that this new eviction branch (span_count > 1000 triggering zpopmin) has no test coverage. This is a legitimate missing test concern for newly added nontrivial logic - the eviction behavior, boundary conditions, and ordering could regress without detection.
